text:
Yegor Sharangovich has settled into a steady, middle-of-the-lineup role in his fourth season in Calgary: 16 minutes a night, 4 goals and 10 points in 21 games, and a two-point night in Los Angeles on Nov. 14, capped by an empty-net goal, that headlines credited for helping the Flames hold off the Kings.

The picture underneath is mixed. At five-on-five, Calgary takes about 55% of the shot attempts with him on the ice but only about 47% of the chance quality, which means a lot of the volume comes from the outside. His teammates have also scored about four and a half goals fewer than their chances while he's out there, which is bad luck that tends to even out. His own finishing is close to normal: 4 goals on 5.06 expected.

Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, 291st among 401 forwards, after a 15-goal year. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him one clear strength: 71% of his exits leave the zone with the puck. He has a heavy shot, near 90 mph at the top end, and what we'd watch is whether more of it comes from closer in.
headline: Yegor Sharangovich is carrying the shots but not the chances
